title: He was king for one month.
paragraphs: He was king for one month.
One.
And most people scroll right past him.
Shallum barely gets a few verses in Scripture, yet his life screams a warning we still need today: you can grab a throne and still lose your soul.

In 2 Kings 15:10–15, Shallum rises through violence. He conspires against King Zechariah, strikes him down in public, and takes the crown. For a moment, it looks like power won. For a moment, ambition gets what it wanted.
But only for a moment.

Because the throne he stole could not save him. The title he seized could not secure him. And the kingdom he grasped slipped through his fingers almost immediately. Another man came, struck him down, and ended his rule after just one month.
That is the tragedy of flesh-driven ambition.
It reaches.
It kills.
It climbs.
And then it collapses.

But here’s what we miss: Shallum is not just a forgotten king in Israel’s history. He is a mirror for every heart that tries to build significance without surrendering to God. Every time we force open a door God did not open… every time we use sin to secure success… every time we crave position more than obedience… we walk in Shallum’s shadow.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Because Jesus is the true King who did not seize a throne by violence. He laid down His life in love. Shallum took a life to wear a crown. Jesus wore a crown of thorns to give life to sinners like us.
That is the Gospel.

Where Shallum grasped, Christ surrendered.
Where Shallum murdered, Christ was pierced.
Where Shallum’s reign lasted a month, Jesus reigns forever.

So if your heart has been chasing recognition, control, or power apart from God, do not harden yourself. Repent. Come back. The mercy of Christ is stronger than your ambition and deeper than your failure.
Some people are forgotten because they seemed small.
Shallum is remembered because his sin was loud.
But Jesus can redeem both the overlooked and the corrupt.
Even now.
The character I almost overlooked became a warning I could not ignore.
Read Shallum again. Then look to Christ.
Scripture: 2 Kings 15:10–15
